skill.name: infsh-cli
skill.description: Use the inference.sh belt CLI to discover and run cloud AI apps for images, video, text, search, audio, 3D, and Twitter/X actions.
skill.summary: Run inference.sh cloud AI apps from the belt CLI.
skill.author: qu-skills

security_audit.summary: The most serious confirmed issue is repeated pipe-to-shell installation from a remote URL, which is a critical supply-chain execution pattern. Several Markdown command examples are safe documentation, but the skill also enables remote app execution, local file uploads, and Twitter/X write actions that need explicit user confirmation.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly into sh.
remediation.suggestion: Make manual download with checksum and signature verification the primary install path, and require explicit confirmation before any remote installer execution.

remediation.issue: Local file paths are uploaded to cloud apps.
remediation.suggestion: Before running any command with a local path, list the exact files, explain the destination, and ask for user approval.

remediation.issue: Twitter/X write actions can publish externally.
remediation.suggestion: Require a final confirmation before posting, direct messaging, following, liking, or reposting through any X/Twitter app.

remediation.issue: Related skill installation expands the trusted instruction surface.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid automatic npx skill installation and ask users to review the source, permissions, and maintainer before adding related skills.

remediation.issue: API key guidance can lead to accidental secret exposure.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend secret managers or scoped CI variables, and warn users not to place API keys in shared prompts, logs, or command history.

content.user_title: Run AI Apps from the inference.sh CLI
content.value_statement: Teams need one command path for many cloud AI models. This skill helps users find apps, prepare inputs, run jobs, and track results with the belt CLI.
actual_capabilities: Guides installation and authentication for the inference.sh belt CLI.
Shows how to browse, search, and inspect public AI apps.
Runs AI apps with inline input or saved input files.
Explains local file uploads for image, video, audio, and media workflows.
Tracks long-running tasks and saves generated results.
Documents app categories including LLMs, search, image, video, 3D, and Twitter/X.
limitations: Requires the belt CLI, an inference.sh account, and available account credits.
Commands send prompts, inputs, and selected files to inference.sh or connected providers.
The skill does not verify every third-party app schema before execution.
Twitter/X write actions can publish externally and need explicit user approval.

use_cases.title: Generate media assets
use_cases.description: Create images, videos, audio, or 3D assets from prompts using hosted inference.sh apps.

use_cases.title: Run model experiments
use_cases.description: Compare LLM, search, and media apps from one CLI during prototyping.

use_cases.title: Automate cloud AI jobs
use_cases.description: Submit long-running jobs, check task status, and save generated results for workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Find an app
prompt_templates.prompt: Find inference.sh apps for image generation and explain which one fits a simple product mockup task.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a run
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me inspect an inference.sh app, create a sample input file, and run it with a short prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Use local media
prompt_templates.prompt: Run an inference.sh app with a local image file. Show me the files that will be uploaded before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Build a tracked workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a belt CLI workflow that submits a video generation job, returns the task ID, checks progress, and saves the final output.

output_examples.input: Find a fast video generation app and prepare a first run.
output: Suggested app: google/veo-3-1-fast for short video generation.
Next step: inspect the app details, create a sample input file, then run with your prompt.
Safety note: review cost and provider terms before submitting the job.

output_examples.input: Run an upscaler on a local product image.
output: The local image path will be uploaded to inference.sh for processing.
I would ask for confirmation before uploading the file.

output_examples.input: Check the result of a long-running generation task.
output_examples.output: The skill can retrieve the task status, show whether it is complete, and save the resulting media link when available.

best_practices: Confirm account, cost, and provider terms before running paid or third-party apps.
Review every local file path before upload, especially private media or customer data.
Require explicit approval before any Twitter/X posting, direct messaging, following, liking, or reposting.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote install scripts to a shell without reviewing and verifying them.
Do not place API keys, private prompts, or customer data directly in shared command history.
Do not run social media write actions without a clear user request and final confirmation.

faq.question: What CLI does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses the inference.sh belt CLI to discover apps, run jobs, and retrieve task results.

faq.question: Does it require an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: Yes. Users must authenticate with belt login or provide an API key for automation.

faq.question: Can it upload local files?
faq.answer: Yes. Some commands accept local paths, and the CLI uploads those files for cloud processing.

faq.question: Can it post to Twitter/X?
faq.answer: The documented app examples include Twitter/X write actions. These should require explicit approval before execution.

faq.question: Does it run apps locally?
faq.answer: No. It submits jobs to inference.sh cloud apps and retrieves the resulting output.

faq.question: Is raw installer execution required?
faq.answer: No. The skill documents a pipe-to-shell installer and a manual download path. Manual verification is safer.
